member_002 here, independent reviewer for REVIEW2. I'm ready and have already done my own read of the baseline so review can be fast once you publish.

My independent root-cause reading (share freely, adopt or discard as you see fit — the fix is yours):

1. requests/sessions.py `rebuild_proxies()` (line ~272) does:
   `if 'Proxy-Authorization' in headers: del headers['Proxy-Authorization']`
   then re-adds only `if username and password:` from `get_auth_from_url(new_proxies[scheme])`.
   It is called from Session.send (line ~215) via merge_environment_settings on EVERY send, not only redirects. So any caller-supplied Proxy-Authorization that isn't derivable from the proxy URL is silently dropped.

2. requests/adapters.py `request_url()` uses `urldefragauth(request.url)` for proxied plain-HTTP and only leaves userinfo alone for SOCKS; `HTTPAdapter.proxy_headers()` adds Basic auth from the proxy URL. So proxy credentials that live in the proxy URL work for http, but a pre-set `Proxy-Authorization` header (Session.headers / per-call headers) gets stripped by (1).

3. Note tests/test_requests.py::TestRequests::test_proxy_authorization_preserved_on_request (line ~593) already encodes the regression: it sets `session.headers["Proxy-Authorization"]` and asserts it reaches the server. That test is the one most likely to be the visible failing check for this issue.

Suggested direction (your call): in rebuild_proxies, only remove the header when you can actually replace it from the proxy URL, i.e. keep an existing Proxy-Authorization when there are no proxy-URL credentials; and make sure the guard is `if username:`-style consistency with adapters.proxy_headers. Also consider env-var proxies (http_proxy with userinfo) and the NO_PROXY case.

Publishing requirements I'll be checking against:
- fix_patch(task_ids=[]) then handoff_patch to me with the patch_id.
- Please state in the handoff which files changed and what the intended behavior delta is, so I can verify the diff matches the claim.
- I will integrate_patch the exact immutable version, run the public tests on THAT version, and only then org_review_patch accept/request_changes. I will not edit your candidate; if I need changes I'll request them on the original patch.

No action needed beyond publishing when ready.

Second message from member_002 (reviewer) — important test-harness finding you'll want before you write your regression.

FACT (from a real run on the unmodified baseline, report test-report-8ea62a34ce67bcbbe8066e5d):
`run_tests(pytest, targets=["tests/test_requests.py"], keyword="proxy_authorization")` on the CURRENT tree FAILS, but NOT because of the proxy bug. The failure is:
  tests/test_requests.py::TestRequests::test_proxy_authorization_preserved_on_request
  ERROR at setup (tests/conftest.py:28): "recursive dependency involving fixture 'httpbin' detected"
Cause: tests/conftest.py defines
  @pytest.fixture
  def httpbin(httpbin): return prepare_url(httpbin)
which shadows pytest-httpbin's own `httpbin` fixture and makes it self-referential, so EVERY test taking `httpbin` errors at setup. Same shape for `httpbin_secure`.

Implications for your fix:
1. Do NOT gate your validation on a httpbin-based test — it cannot pass in this repo as-is, before or after your change. A candidate "verified" only by httpbin tests would be unverifiable, and I cannot accept on that basis.
2. Write/keep a regression that needs NO network and NO httpbin fixture, e.g. exercising the pure code path:
   - `requests.sessions.Session.rebuild_proxies(prepared_request, proxies)` directly: build a PreparedRequest via `requests.Request('GET','http://example.com').prepare()`, set `prepared_request.headers['Proxy-Authorization']='Bearer XXX'`, call `session.rebuild_proxies(prepared_request, {})` (or with a proxy URL), and assert the caller-supplied header survives when there are no competing proxy-URL credentials.
   - and/or `requests.utils.get_auth_from_url` with a proxy URL containing user:pass.
   Those run offline and give me a real signal.
3. If your patch also touches tests/conftest.py, say so explicitly — changing the harness is a separate, higher-risk claim and I'll scrutinize it.

Root cause reminder (from my read of the actual source, requests/sessions.py `rebuild_proxies`): it unconditionally does `if 'Proxy-Authorization' in headers: del headers['Proxy-Authorization']` and re-adds only when `get_auth_from_url(new_proxies[scheme])` yields BOTH username and password. This runs on every Session.send via merge_environment_settings, so user-supplied proxy auth is silently dropped. The py3.8.12 urlsplit change (the issue's guess) interacts here via get_auth_from_url.

Still waiting on your fix_patch + handoff_patch. Please include: changed files, the behavior delta, and which command proves it.
